rationale: New schema binds every manifest field (including commit/time/schema/producer), component path/type/size/BLAKE3 and the exact selected artifact inventory. Bytes are re-read from the explicit external root through nofollow descriptors. Domain-separated ECDSA P256/SHA256 covers the full canonical manifest, checked only with an external trust key. Legacy causal-hash signatures cannot establish this binding and are rejected, not upgraded. Tampered metadata, rehashed manifests, source changes and wrong signature representations are rejected in confined tests.

rationale: The verifier reads artifact.sha256 and compares it only with manifest.artifact_hash, then labels ARTIFACT HASH VERIFIED. The generator hashes actual source files, but the verifier neither accepts an artifact/root input nor recomputes that aggregate. An unchanged bundle can therefore verify its recorded digest independently of changed artifact bytes. This is a binding/wording limitation of the verifier, not evidence that a signature was forged. Re-reviewed after Lot4: the new producer emits v3 selected-file snapshots with a new portable verifier; it does not regenerate or fix this historical v2 verifier. Its string-only artifact check remains and C0135 stays OPEN/P2. The cross-source reference is refreshed because the old producer was replaced, not because this copy was fixed.

source_checks.observation: Required files include digest metadata, not the underlying source artifact set.
Artifact check compares strings and incorporates that recorded digest into the joint digest.
Output calls that result ARTIFACT HASH VERIFIED.
Current wrapper produces a different contract; the separately stored historical v2 verifier is unchanged.

guards: Joint digest and signature can authenticate the recorded artifact hash; they do not verify the current artifact bytes.
Verifier is useful for detached bundle consistency, but that scope should not be presented as checking current artifacts.
